claims.text: The initial microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Optimizing lamellar colony size through hierarchical microstructure design will improve strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
Optimizing internal boundary density through hierarchical microstructure design will improve strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
Optimizing lamellar colony size through hierarchical microstructure design will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified baseline.
Optimizing internal boundary density through hierarchical microstructure design will improve room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified baseline.
Optimized lamellar colony size and internal boundary density will reduce microcrack initiation.
Optimized lamellar colony size and internal boundary density will reduce microcrack propagation.
Reduced microcrack initiation and propagation will enhance strength.
Reduced microcrack initiation and propagation will enhance room-temperature tensile ductility.
The proposed intervention is applicable within the constraints of conventional processing and previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies.
The exact relationship among lamellar colony size, internal boundary density, and mechanical properties is uncertain.
Failure to improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
